title: Norm-one retraction onto a finite ell-adic subfield
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extending nonarchimedean absolute value and its norm topology [def-weil-algebraic-closure], [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and a finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. There exists an $F$-linear map $p_F:\Omega\to F$ with $p_F(a)=a$ for $a\in F$ and $|p_F(x)|\leq |x|$ for every $x\in\Omega$. In particular it is continuous. No completeness of $\Omega$ is assumed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel expansion: uniformly bounded finite-field projections for a pointwise finite coefficient decomposition; agent-formulated auxiliary lemma, exact literature reference WANTED.

proof.text: Use the inherited norm on the intermediate field F. It is the restriction of the ambient norm by construction, so the inclusion F → Ω is isometric without invoking uniqueness of an extending absolute value. F is a normed vector space of finite dimension over Q_l. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-proper], implemented by FiniteDimensional.proper, F is proper and its closed balls are compact. The ultrametric inequality on Ω restricts to F. Let i : F →ₗ[F] Ω be the algebra map and identify F with its range W by the injective linear equivalence e. The inverse f = e.symm is linear and satisfies |f(w)| = ||w|| because inclusion preserves norms.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the norm-one finite-field projection input

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-admissible-scalar-balls] with $K=F$ and $V=\Omega$. The field absolute value and vector norm satisfy its axioms by step 1, and its compact-ball hypothesis holds there. Thus for every $F$-subspace $U\subseteq\Omega$, every contractive $F$-linear $g:U\to F$, and every $x\notin U$, there is $b\in F$ with $|b-g(u)|\leq\|x-u\|$ for all $u\in U$. This is exactly the scalar-value condition, including all partial maps, required in the next step.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel projection input; assembly after the Q91 re-split.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-contractive-extension-from-admissible-values] to K=F and V=Ω, using nnnorm for the scalar absolute value and vector norm. Normed-field laws supply nondegeneracy, the value at one, multiplication, and scalar homogeneity; step 1 supplies the ultrametric inequalities. The scalar-value hypothesis is step 2. Take W to be the range of i and f=e.symm as in step 1, with its isometric bound. The resulting linear map h : Ω →ₗ[F] F agrees with e.symm on W, hence h(i(a))=a for every a∈F, and satisfies ||h(x)||≤||x||.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel projection input; assembly after the Q91 re-split.

proof.text: Turn h into a continuous linear map by LinearMap.mkContinuous with constant 1, using ||h(x)||≤1*||x||. Its underlying function is unchanged, so evaluating the extension identity at e(a) proves it fixes every a∈F. The same bound gives the second asserted clause. This is the Lipschitz continuity argument, and it uses no completeness of Ω.
